title: Royalties lost: the Zoot Sims album and Buck Hill
summary: He got nothing from the Zoot Sims album; Schremp tells how little record royalties pay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: When you're down next month-- I really wish I knew how to do this properly, get after all these
You know, this album that I wrote for Zoot Sims, the four altos--
I heard one cut out of it, I never heard the whole album.
I have it; I'll play it for you.

But anyway, that album was sold out in this country, the second printing was sold out, then it was reprinted in England and sold out. It's hard to get. I never got penny one from that, and it's all original music, it's all my music; not one cent.
How did that happen, you didn't have a contract with them?
It happened. The publishers are out of business; I don't know what to do about it.

Buck Hill, a great tenor player down in Washington, will make a record for Inner City, and he'll get a fee, he'll get a thousand dollars or whatever, and then, before he starts making any royalty money, he has, out of his own royalties, has to pay for the whole production costs and by the time he's worked out all the studio costs and the other band players, all the other costs and the first thing is sold out and he'll get seventeen dollars, and unless they go to second pressing, that's it--
(Side A of Tape 3 ended at this point. Transcript will continue in accordance with Side B.)
